1. List has been revised.

3. Supplementary affidavit filed today by the learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material available on record.

sentences.text: Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 247 of 2023, under Sections 376, 506 of I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station - Narkhi, District - Firozabad, during the pendency of trial.

PROSECUTION STORY:
6. The FIR was instituted by the informant stating that her daughter aged about 15 years was gang raped by the applicant and his brohter Shilendra and one Raghubeer on 06.03.2023 at about 01:00 am at the agricultural field.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
7.
The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.
8. The FIR is delayed by about three months and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
9. Even the application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was moved after a delay of two months i.e. on 11.05.2023.
10. The instant FIR is just a counter blast to FIR No.25 of 2023 instituted by the sister-in-law (bhabhi) of the informant against the husband of the informant.
11. There is no medical corroboration of the incident.
12. It is a clear cut case of false implication.
13. The age of the victim has deliberately been suppressed to coerce the applicant into compromise in the said FIR No.25 of 2023.

14. Even the statement of the victim recorded by the doctor conducting her medical examination does not mention the name of any other accused person except the applicant, as such, it is contradictory to the FIR.
15. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.

16. The applicant is languishing in jail since 26.08.2024, having no criminal history to his credit,
deserves to be released on bail.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE:

sentences.text: The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

CONCLUSION:
18. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

19. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
20.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view, the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595, has again emphasized that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
21.
Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
22. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

23. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, pending trial and considering the complicity of accused, severity of punishment, at this stage, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

24. Let the applicant- Komal Singh, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to Komal Singh vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22150032/
3 treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

26. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
